To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

people with mental illnesses are interested in improving the quality of their lives, that they have many ideas about how this can be accomplished, and that they want to be included in the planning and decision-making that will lead to these improvements.

the participants in our study: • Want the mental health system to be responsive to their needs and to be a place where they can feel safe and secure. • Want to have control and choices in their lives, to be treated with dignity and respect, to be listened to, to have their opinions valued, to be treated as an equal and to be given the opportunity to be a contributing member of the community. • Want to be able to live in the community with the supports that they need.
the perspectives of people who live with mental illnesses and their family members on quality of life issues are complex.

the perspectives of people living with mental illnesses and their family members.
the quality of life of people who live with mental illnesses and their family members.
the quality of life of people with mental illness and their families, and the factors that affect this.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
quality of life for people with mental illness is not only a matter of the individual's own perceptions, but is also a matter of how others perceive the person and how they treat the person.
quality of life is a complex and multifaceted concept, which is difficult to define and measure.
the findings from this study support the need for policy makers to continue to support the recovery process for individuals living with serious mental illness and their family members.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quality of life is a complex issue for people living with mental illnesses and their family members.

the quality of life for people with mental illnesses is enhanced when they are able to live in their own home, have access to meaningful employment and social relationships, and have the support of family members.
quality of life is a multidimensional concept that is highly individualized and that is influenced by the interaction between individuals living with mental illness and their service system. (Author)

people living with mental illnesses and their families are experts on their own lives and their experiences.
quality of life for individuals with mental illnesses and their families is a complex, multidimensional concept that cannot be adequately captured by a single measure.
